messages:
alex: Morning — I ran the new kernel-sampler schedule overnight on gpu-pool-03. Canary shows a ~12% p99 regression for seqlen=512 workloads when using torch.compile + cudaGraph warmup. KV-cache hit rate unchanged. Any quick ideas? :thinking:

maria: sampler as in the probabilistic selection that explores alternate kernels during warmup? can you paste the profile output? :eyes:

alex: yep — sampler.explore=true during warmup. Pasted top lines from perf-bot below.
perf-bot: ```
profile: sampler-run/2026-03-17
model: rdlw-7b.fp16
config: sampler.schedule=adaptive, explore=true, threshold=0.6
seqlen=512, batch=1
baseline (no sampler): p50=12ms p95=28ms p99=45ms
with sampler: p50=11.5ms p95=30ms p99=50.4ms
kv_cache_hits=98.7%
observed kernel_ids during warmup: [k_fp16_fast, k_int8_sparse, k_fp16_fast]
cudaGraph captures: captured kernel=k_fp16_fast
replay later swapped to k_int8_sparse -> fallback cost observed
```
jordan: that sequence is suspicious — if the capture recorded fp16 path but sampler swapped to int8 later, cudagraph replay will mismatch and force fallback/reshuffle which kills tail latency. Did we pin kernel_id during capture?
sara: we saw a similar flake last month. The sampler's stochastic flips can change layout/kernel choice after capture. Two mitigations worked: 1) disable exploration for the capture window, 2) force the capture to use the deterministic selection (kernel_id pin).
alex: sharing minimal repro (pseudo):
```
with torch.compile(model):
  for i in range(warmup_iters):
    out = model(inp)
  torch.cuda.CUDAGraph().capture()
  # if sampler flips between warmup and capture you'll capture different kernel
```
plus sampler config: `{"sampler.explore": true, "sampler.threshold": 0.6}`

maria: quick triage: run canary that sets sampler.explore=false during capture and keeps explore=true afterwards. or bump threshold so the int8 path isn't chosen for seqlen=512. also add a small validation run that asserts captured kernel_id == runtime kernel_id on replay.
jordan: also consider adding a capture-guard that rejects captures if sampling entropy > epsilon (we already emit a metric sampler.entropy). Could fail capture-fast to avoid a bad cudagraph.
alex: I'll run a canary now with explore=false in the capture window and an assertion check. Will post results. Thanks — saving the perf logs. :thumbsup:
